proposals.hypothesis: The best recipe (38.596) may be over-regularized or under-regularized. This parameter-only ablation tests a slightly higher learning rate (0.05) and lower regularization (reg_lambda=5) to see if the model can capture more signal. It avoids the 'broad' feature failure by keeping the proven 'missing' feature set.

The 'broad' feature set failed because generic features added noise. This feature-only ablation adds two explicit interaction features: floor_area * heating_degree_days and floor_area * cooling_degree_days. These capture the physical relationship between building size and weather-driven energy demand, avoiding the noise of generic features.

The best recipe (38.60) uses colsample_bytree ~0.99, implying high feature correlation and potential overfitting to specific weather combinations; reducing feature sampling to 0.85 will force the model to rely on more robust, generalizable patterns. This addresses the lack of regularization diversity compared to the worse-performing baseline (48.97) which used 0.8.

The current model treats monthly temperatures as independent features, missing the seasonal amplitude and thermal stress dynamics that drive energy consumption; adding seasonal temperature range (max-min) and heating/cooling load proxies will provide explicit signals for HVAC intensity. This addresses the potential under-utilization of temporal weather structure in the 38.60 baseline.
